walkthrough:
Determine the runner's speed at each stage:
- Initial state at $t = 0$: $u = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
- At $t = 5\text{ s}$: $v = at = 1.2 \times 5 = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
- Constant cruising speed: maintains $v = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ from $t = 5\text{ s}$ to $t = 5 + 12 = 17\text{ s}$.
- Deceleration to rest: from $t = 17\text{ s}$ to $t = 17 + 3 = 20\text{ s}$, reaching $v = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Sketch the graph connecting the vertices $(0, 0)$, $(5, 6)$, $(17, 6)$, and $(20, 0)$ with straight line segments on axes $t$ ($0$ to $20$) and $v$ ($0$ to $6$).

Calculate the total displacement as the area under the velocity-time graph:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{a + b}{2} \times h$$
where $a = 12\text{ s}$ (top base), $b = 20\text{ s}$ (bottom base), and $h = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ (height):
$$\text{Distance } PQ = \frac{12 + 20}{2} \times 6 = \frac{32}{2} \times 6 = 16 \times 6 = 96\text{ m}$$

The cyclist's velocity-time graph is a triangle with base $20\text{ s}$ and peak velocity $v_{\text{max}}$.
Divide $v_{\text{max}}$ by the acceleration duration ($10\text{ s}$) to find the acceleration: $a = \frac{v_{\text{max}}}{10}$.
walkthrough:
Identify the parameters of the cyclist's journey:
- Starts from rest at $t = 10\text{ s}$ and finishes at rest at $t = 30\text{ s}$.
- Total duration: $30 - 10 = 20\text{ s}$.
- Accelerates for $10\text{ s}$ to peak velocity $v_{\text{max}}$, then decelerates for the remaining $10\text{ s}$ back to rest.
- Total distance travelled: $s = 96\text{ m}$.

Calculate the peak speed $v_{\text{max}}$ using the triangular area under the cyclist's graph:
$$\text{Distance} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$$
$$96 = \frac{1}{2} \times 20 \times v_{\text{max}}$$
$$96 = 10v_{\text{max}}$$
Divide by $10$:
$$v_{\text{max}} = \frac{96}{10} = 9.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Calculate the acceleration from the rate of change of velocity:
$$a = \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}$$
Substitute $\Delta v = 9.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $\Delta t = 10\text{ s}$:
$$a = \frac{9.6}{10} = 0.96\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
